title: Move a coated wafer from the spin coater into a single-wafer case and lock it shut
instruction: Use the tweezers to take the wafer off the spin coater and lay it, pattern side up, in the case lid. Then put the domed case bottom on with its arrow at OPEN and turn it to LOCK. Never touch the wafer's top or hold the wafer with the gripper.
context: After spin coating, a technician lifts the wafer off the chuck by its edge with wafer tweezers and seals it in a single-wafer case for storage or transport; the coated top must never be touched.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. Spin coater (fixed): white housing 22 x 22 x 4 cm centred at (0.31, -0.12), with a round catch bowl 19 cm across inside a ribbed wall 3.2 cm high, and a black vacuum chuck 2.4 cm across, its top 5.2 cm above the table, at the centre; its clear lid, hinged along the back edge, stands open past upright against its stop. On the chuck, centred, pattern side up: a 2-inch silicon wafer, 50.8 mm across, 1 mm thick, 4 g. Wafer tweezers (stainless steel, 20 g) standing tips down in a grey cup at (0.17, -0.27): two 8 x 2.5 mm arms 85 mm long, ending in blades 14 mm wide and 12 mm long bent 45 degrees, sprung open 5 mm; the cup is 21.5 x 17 mm inside and 3.5 cm deep, its floor 2 cm above the table. Single-wafer case (polypropylene), in two pieces: its lid, open side up, centred at (0.15, 0.02): a 92 mm disc 2 mm thick with 14 pins (2.4 mm across, 3 mm tall) on a 47 mm circle that the wafer rests on, and a wall 7 mm high and 2 mm thick on a 57 mm circle, both open over about 60 degrees towards the robots (-x) for the tweezers' blades; red OPEN and LOCK marks on the front of its flange, LOCK 30 degrees clockwise of OPEN; 20 g. Its domed bottom, dome up, at (0.20, 0.17): a skirt 75 mm across and 14 mm high under a stepped dome, 20.5 mm tall in all, with a red arrow on the skirt facing the robots; 15 g; it fits over the lid's wall and sits on its flange. Fixed layout matching the screenshot.
scoring: Measured at the end. 0 if at any time: a fingertip came within 6 mm above the wafer's top, more than 3 mm inside its rim (top touched); a fingertip came within 2 mm of the wafer's rim at its height (held by the gripper); or the wafer tilted past 40 degrees or reached the table (dropped). Otherwise, with the wafer lying flat (within 3 degrees) on the lid's pins, its centre within 2.5 mm of the lid's axis: 1.0 if the bottom is seated on the lid's flange (axis within 2.5 mm, within 1.5 mm of seated height, within 3 degrees of level), was set on within 10 degrees of the OPEN mark and then turned 22 to 45 degrees clockwise without being lifted, and both hands are at least 8 cm from the case's axis; 0.5 if the bottom is seated but not locked, or a hand is still at the case; 0.25 if the bottom is not seated. 0 if the wafer is not on the lid's pins.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Open the case, put the wafer back on the chuck (centred, pattern up), the tweezers back in their cup and the case's two pieces back as in the screenshot; leave the coater's lid open against its stop.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz. The wafer is rigid, drawn 1 mm thick (real 0.28 mm), and cannot chip; the chuck's vacuum is off. The tweezers are two halves on a sprung slide, not a bending spring. The bayonet is not modelled: the bottom rests on the lid and locking is scored from its turn. The lid grips the bench (friction 1.0) better than the bottom grips the lid (0.25). Touching the wafer is scored from fingertip positions, not contact.
